newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares gain but cautious, blue chips active.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares gain but cautious, blue chips active.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded higher on Tuesday but lagged behind gains on other markets following the surge in the United States a day earlier.
Dealers said the market was cautious following a mixed bag of first quarter results, although volume was healthy and interest in blue chips high.
Pharmaceuticals group Nycomed took a plunge, falling 6.6 percent to close at 99 crowns, while the B stock slid 5.2 percent to 96 crowns.
Dealers attributed the move to results of German drugs company Schering and pressure in the contrast agents' market.

Fokus Bank was the most traded share in turnover terms due to internal transfers from takeover bidder Sparebankgruppen. Fokus accounted for 76.8 million crowns in turnover but ended unchanged at 66 crowns per share.
Turnover was a high 44.6 million crowns in technology group Nera, which ended one crown down at 41. "People are still trying to make up their minds about Nera," said a broker.

Oslo's Total index advanced 0.44 percent to 1,118 points in turnover of 1.19 billion crowns. "The market has been very good today. There was a lot of trading in blue chips and overall a good volume," commented one broker.
